title: Basic SELECTS [WHERE clause]
description:
Sometimes, you don't want all ROWS of the data either. This is where the WHERE clause comes up. WHERE only selects the data where the condition is true. To actually make a condition, let me cover the 2 most basic oerators, = and !=. = is true when left is equal to right, and != is true when left is not right. An example of a SELECT with WHERE is: 
```sql
-- Let's say we have a table users with columns name and age and rows steve, 21 and bob 24: To select only name when age is equal to 21, you would do:
SELECT name FROM users WHERE age = 21;
```
